{{Quote|It's a Kuati Signet. Blue kyber. Sky stone. The ancient world. Celebrates the uprising against the Rakatan invaders.|[[Luthen Rael]], to [[Cassian Jeron Andor]]|<ref name="Aldhani">{{Andor|Aldhani (episode)}}</ref>}}
The '''Rakatans''',<ref name="100 Objects">''[[Star Wars 100 Objects]]''</ref> also known as the '''Rakata''', were an ancient [[Amphibian|amphibious]] [[humanoid]] [[species]] native to the [[planet]] [[Rakata Prime|Lehon]]<ref name="BMF" /> who ruled over the so-called [[Infinite Empire]].<ref name="NoP">''[[Nexus of Power]]''</ref> According to legend, they were the first to develop [[hyperspace]] travel.<ref name="BMF" /> Long before the [[Imperial Era]], the Rakatans staged an [[Invasion of Kuat|invasion]] of the planet [[Kuat]], but were eventually repelled by an [[Uprising against the Rakatan invaders|uprising]].<ref name="sw100">''[[Star Wars 100 Objects]]''</ref> A [[Kuati Signet]] embedded with a [[Color|blue]] [[kyber crystal]] commemorated the uprising.<ref name="Aldhani" /> Around [[25,000 BBY]], Rakatan invaders also [[Sacking of Chandrila|sacked]] the planet [[Chandrila]] and stole the twelve [[Chandi Merle]] statues that stood in one of their temples around the same [[Standard year|year]].<ref name="Harvest">{{Andor|Harvest}}</ref> The Rakatan species was said to have eventually gone extinct as a result of corruption from the [[dark side of the Force]].<ref name="BMF" /> They shared their name with mystical antiquities known as [[Rakatan wraith box]]es.<ref name="Solo Official Guide">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]''</ref>

{{Species-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
===Canon and origins===
[[File:Rakata_profile.png|thumb|right|A Rakata in ''Star Wars'' Legends]]
The Rakatans were first mentioned in the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in the [[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 45|forty-fifth issue]] of the [[De Agostini]] magazine ''[[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon]]'', albeit only in its German release.<ref name="BMF 45">{{BuildFalconCite|45|Guide to the Galaxy}}</ref> The species originated in [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] in the [[2003]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''. The [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] in that game were the fallen remnant of what had once been a galaxy-spanning [[Infinite Empire/Legends|empire]] that conquered, ruled, and decimated other species through the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]].<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> [[The Force/Legends|The Force]] powered the Rakata's [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] technology.<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

===Inconsistencies===
====''Star Wars'' series====
{{Quote|What a time for a light failure...|Unidentified Mon Calamari|<ref name="SW48">[[Star Wars (2015) 48|''Star Wars'' (2015) 48]]</ref>}}
[[File:RakatanOnMonCala-2015StarWars48.jpg|thumb|left|125px|A Mon Calamari in ''Star Wars'' (2015) 48]]
In the [[Star Wars (2015) 48|forty-eighth issue]] of the [[2015]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series ''[[Star Wars (2015)|Star Wars]]'', written by [[Kieron Gillen]], penciled by [[Salvador Larroca]], and published by [[Marvel Comics]]<ref name="SW48" /> on [[May 23]], [[2018]],<ref name="Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/67554/star_wars_2015_48|text=Star Wars (2015) #48}}</ref> an unidentified [[Mon Calamari]] from the script<ref name="Matt tweet">{{Twitter|missingwords|status/999452002324131841|[[Matt Martin]]|date=2018-05-24|quote=Yeah, you're not the only one to say that. I'd say it could be an alien extra who may or may not be a Rakata. But it's not DEFINITELY a Rakata. And like I said, the script calls out a Mon Cal but it's not stated in the issue specifically.|archiveurl=https://archive.is/9nq4C|archivefile=File:MattMartin-StarWars48RakataError-Twitter.png}} {{C|In response to: "But I'm not crazy, right? That guy totally looks like a Rakata, right????"}}</ref> was mistakenly depicted as a member of the Rakatan species.<ref name="SW48" />

====''Poe Dameron'' series====
{{Quote|I don't even remember that dude and I'm pretty sure I would have remembered approving a Rakata.|Matt Martin|<ref name="that dude #3457">{{Twitter|missingwords|status/953908823890079744|[[Matt Martin]]|date=2018-01-18|quote=I don't even remember that dude and I'm pretty sure I would have remembered approving a Rakata. He's "generic alien extra #3457" as far as I'm concerned. Could he be retconned to be a Rakata, sure. But as of now, he's just some mysterious background guy.|archiveurl=https://archive.is/U8RGM|archivefile=File:MattMartin-PoeDameronRakata-Twitter.png}} {{C|In response to: "Is this like the Rakata that "supposedly" appeared on the Poe comic? Or that was identified as a Rakata? I keep saying that is not."}}</ref>}}
[[File:Rakata-PoeDameron7.png|thumb|right|125px|"Generic alien extra #3457" in ''Poe Dameron'' 7]]
Likewise, in the [[Poe Dameron 7|seventh issue]] of the [[2016]] comic book series ''[[Star Wars: Poe Dameron]]'', written by [[Charles Soule]], penciled by [[Angel Unzueta]], and published by Marvel Comics<ref name="Poe7">[[Poe Dameron 7|''Poe Dameron'' 7]]</ref> on [[October 26]], [[2016]],<ref name="NewsaramaDelay">{{WebCite|url=https://www.newsarama.com/30519-darth-vader-han-solo-more-star-wars-titles-delayed.html|text=DARTH VADER, HAN SOLO, More STAR WARS Titles Delayed|date=2016-08-05|archivedate=20200210012746}}</ref> an unidentified "thug"<ref name="Poe7" /> who was dubbed "generic alien extra #3457" and described as "mysterious background guy" by [[Lucasfilm Story Group|Story Group's]] [[Matt Martin]] on [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]],<ref name="that dude #3457" /> was also depicted resembling the Rakatans,<ref name="Poe7" /> but their species remained unspecified.<ref name="that dude #3457" />
